bucket_name.description:
The resource name of the Log Bucket that owns the Log Metric. Only Log Buckets in projects
are supported. The bucket has to be in the same project as the metric.
bucket_name.rationale: Bucket name identifies which log bucket contains the metric. Has no direct security impact.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

description.description:
A description of this metric, which is used in documentation. The maximum length of the
description is 8000 characters.
description.rationale: Description is metadata only and does not affect security controls.

disabled.description: If set to True, then this metric is disabled and it does not generate any points.
disabled.rationale: Security metrics must always be active to monitor critical events. Disabling metrics creates blind spots for IAM changes, firewall changes, and other security-critical events. CIS GCP Benchmark requires active alerting.

filter.description:
An advanced logs filter (https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/view/advanced-filters) which
is used to match log entries.
filter.rationale: The advanced-logs filter expression that selects which log entries this log-based metric counts. A generic policy cannot meaningfully constrain a free-form filter expression without hardcoding specific filter strings, so it is not a useful policy target; the current text contradicts its own false call by arguing for mandated content.

label_extractors.description:
A map from a label key string to an extractor expression which is used to extract data from a log
entry field and assign as the label value. Each label key specified in the LabelDescriptor must
have an associated extractor expression in this map. The syntax of the extractor expression is
the same as for the valueExtractor field.
label_extractors.rationale: Label extractors define how label values are derived from log entries. No direct security impact.

name.description:
The client-assigned metric identifier. Examples - "error_count", "nginx/requests".
Metric identifiers are limited to 100 characters and can include only the following
characters A-Z, a-z, 0-9, and the special characters _-.,+!*',()%/. The forward-slash
character (/) denotes a hierarchy of name pieces, and it cannot be the first character
of the name.
name.rationale: Name is an identifier for the metric. Has no security implications beyond uniqueness and clarity.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Project identifies where the metric is created. No direct security impact.

value_extractor.description:
A valueExtractor is required when using a distribution logs-based metric to extract the values to
record from a log entry. Two functions are supported for value extraction - EXTRACT(field) or
REGEXP_EXTRACT(field, regex). The argument are 1. field - The name of the log entry field from which
the value is to be extracted. 2. regex - A regular expression using the Google RE2 syntax
(https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax) with a single capture group to extract data from the specified
log entry field. The value of the field is converted to a string before applying the regex. It is an
error to specify a regex that does not include exactly one capture group.
value_extractor.rationale: Value extractor defines how metric values are derived. No direct security impact.

bucket_options.description:
The bucketOptions are required when the logs-based metric is using a DISTRIBUTION value type and it
describes the bucket boundaries used to create a histogram of the extracted values.

bucket_options.explicit_buckets.description: Specifies a set of buckets with arbitrary widths.

bucket_options.explicit_buckets.bounds.description: The values must be monotonically increasing.
bucket_options.explicit_buckets.bounds.rationale: Defines bucket boundaries. No security impact.

bucket_options.exponential_buckets.description:
Specifies an exponential sequence of buckets that have a width that is proportional to the value of
the lower bound. Each bucket represents a constant relative uncertainty on a specific value in the bucket.

bucket_options.exponential_buckets.growt.rationale: Defines bucket growth rate. No security impact.

bucket_options.exponential_buckets.scale.rationale: Defines bucket scaling. No security impact.

bucket_options.linear_buckets.description:
Specifies a linear sequence of buckets that all have the same width (except overflow and underflow).
Each bucket represents a constant absolute uncertainty on the specific value in the bucket.

bucket_options.linear_buckets.offset.description: Lower bound of the first bucket.
bucket_options.linear_buckets.offset.rationale: Defines bucket starting point. No security impact.

bucket_options.linear_buckets.width.rationale: Defines bucket width. No security impact.

metric_descriptor.description:
The optional metric descriptor associated with the logs-based metric.
If unspecified, it uses a default metric descriptor with a DELTA metric kind,
INT64 value type, with no labels and a unit of "1". Such a metric counts the
number of log entries matching the filter expression.

metric_descriptor.display_name.description:
A concise name for the metric, which can be displayed in user interfaces. Use sentence case
without an ending period, for example "Request count". This field is optional but it is
recommended to be set for any metrics associated with user-visible concepts, such as Quota.
metric_descriptor.display_name.rationale: Display name is for UI presentation. Has no security implications.

metric_descriptor.metric_kind.description:
Whether the metric records instantaneous values, changes to a value, etc.
Some combinations of metricKind and valueType might not be supported.
For counter metrics, set this to DELTA. Possible values: ["DELTA", "GAUGE", "CUMULATIVE"]
metric_descriptor.metric_kind.rationale: Metric kind defines measurement behavior. Has no security implications.

metric_descriptor.unit.description:
The unit in which the metric value is reported. It is only applicable if the valueType is
'INT64', 'DOUBLE', or 'DISTRIBUTION'. The supported units are a subset of
[The Unified Code for Units of Measure](http://unitsofmeasure.org/ucum.html) standard
metric_descriptor.unit.rationale: Unit defines measurement scale. Has no security implications.

metric_descriptor.value_type.description:
Whether the measurement is an integer, a floating-point number, etc.
Some combinations of metricKind and valueType might not be supported.
For counter metrics, set this to INT64. Possible values: ["BOOL", "INT64", "DOUBLE", "STRING", "DISTRIBUTION", "MONEY"]
metric_descriptor.value_type.rationale: Value type defines data format. Has no security implications.

metric_descriptor.labels.description:
The set of labels that can be used to describe a specific instance of this metric type. For
example, the appengine.googleapis.com/http/server/response_latencies metric type has a label
for the HTTP response code, response_code, so you can look at latencies for successful responses
or just for responses that failed.

metric_descriptor.labels.description.description: A human-readable description for the label.

metric_descriptor.labels.key.rationale: Label key identifier. No security impact.

metric_descriptor.labels.value_type.description: The type of data that can be assigned to the label. Default value: "STRING" Possible values: ["BOOL", "INT64", "STRING"]
